practices.practice: Keep the cluster connection string and any credentials out of source control and read DOCUMENTDB_URI (or equivalent) from environment variables or a secrets store rather than embedding them in code or committed files.
practices.prior_belief: Keep the cluster connection string and any credentials out of source control: read DOCUMENTDB_URI (and any user/password) from environment variables or a secrets store (e.g., Azure Key Vault) and provide a .env.example placeholder instead of real values.

practices.practice: Always connect with TLS enabled and do not disable certificate validation in production (ensure tls=true and system CA bundle or CA path is configured).
practices.prior_belief: Always connect with TLS/SSL enabled and verify server certificates (do not disable certificate validation) when creating the MongoDB-compatible client (e.g., pass tls=true/tlsCAFile or equivalent driver options).

practices.practice: Instantiate and reuse a single MongoClient per process (module-level singleton) instead of creating a client per request, so the connection pool and topology monitor are shared.
practices.prior_belief: Use the official MongoDB-compatible Python driver (pymongo or a MongoDB 7.0-compatible driver) and instantiate a single MongoClient per process that is reused across threads/requests instead of creating a client per request.

practices.practice: Tune client connection-pool and timeout options (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, maxIdleTimeMS, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) to match workload (serverless vs long-running servers vs OLAP) and avoid frequently creating/closing clients.
practices.prior_belief: Tune client connection-pool options (e.g., maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, socketTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS) appropriate to your concurrency and keep long-lived clients rather than frequent reconnects.

practices.practice: Implement retry semantics for transient errors (rate limits, network blips) using exponential backoff and classify errors to avoid retrying non-idempotent operations without safeguards.
practices.prior_belief: Implement exponential-backoff retries for transient errors (connection/network timeouts, rate-limited responses); classify errors and avoid retrying on non-idempotent failures without safeguards.

practices.practice: Use an explicit, consistent document schema for fraud/transaction data (ids, account references, timestamp, features, embedding vector field and metadata) so code can rely on predictable fields and schemaVersion for migrations.
practices.prior_belief: Use a consistent, explicit schema for fraud documents: include fields transaction_id, account_id, timestamp, features (raw), embedding (fixed-length float32 array), embedding_dim, label (fraud/clean), and any indexed metadata; store embedding in its own field (e.g., embedding_vector).
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB schema best practices; searches: "Azure DocumentDB recommended schema fields for transaction embeddings", "Azure DocumentDB fraud data model example", "cosmos mongodb schema versioning embedding fields"

practices.practice: Ensure all embeddings in a collection use the same dimension and, when using COS (cosine), normalize vectors to unit length at ingestion and store model name + dimensions with each vector.
practices.prior_belief: Ensure all embeddings are the same dimension and record the dimension in each document or collection metadata; if using cosine similarity, pre-normalize vectors to unit length before storing to simplify query-time computation.

practices.practice: Create a cosmosSearch vector index on the vector field and declare its algorithm-specific options (kind, dimensions, similarity and algorithm params such as maxDegree, lBuild, numLists) to match workload and index type.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index best practices

practices.practice: Tune search-time ANN parameters (lSearch/efSearch/efSearch/efSearch vs k, oversampling/probe/nProbes) according to recall/latency needs and keep lSearch >= k; raise lSearch when recall is insufficient.
practices.prior_belief: Tune search-time ANN parameters (e.g., efSearch, probe/nprobe, or topK) per workload: set a conservative topK (e.g., 10–50) and adjust ef/probe to trade recall vs latency; avoid full-table scans in production.

practices.practice: Combine vector similarity with metadata filters by supplying a `filter` inside the `cosmosSearch` operator so predicates are applied during ANN candidate selection rather than post-filtering.
practices.prior_belief: Combine vector similarity with metadata filters (hybrid search) to restrict candidate sets before vector scoring: always apply transaction-date, account-id or other business filters when relevant to limit results and improve precision and cost.

practices.practice: Keep documents small and move very large raw payloads (logs, attachments) to an external blob store with a reference in the document rather than embedding them with vectors.
practices.prior_belief: Limit the size of documents and avoid embedding extremely large objects with vectors; keep embedding vectors lean (float32) and store large raw payloads or logs in a separate blob store with a reference in the document.

practices.practice: Make seeding scripts idempotent by using upsert/replaceOne with upsert:true (or bulk upserts) so repeated runs do not create duplicates and are safe to re-run.
practices.prior_belief: Use upserts or idempotent operations for seed and ingestion scripts (e.g., insert_one with upsert or replace_one with upsert) so repeated runs do not create duplicates and scripts can be safely re-run.
practices.source_name: Manage a document in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB using JavaScript

practices.practice: Avoid building large vector indexes during peak production windows because index build memory/CPU can impact runtime queries; plan builds off-peak or scale resources for the build.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid building large vector indexes in peak-production windows; build indexes in background or on a secondary replica and monitor index-build progress and resource usage.

practices.practice: Provision cluster compute/tier to match expected search and ingestion load (choose appropriate tier such as M30+ for DiskANN/HNSW production vector workloads and scale up when index builds or queries require more memory/CPU).
practices.prior_belief: Provision compute/throughput to match expected search and ingestion load (scale up cluster or choose appropriate compute tier such as M30) and measure RU or CPU usage; avoid under-provisioning index builds or heavy query patterns.

practices.practice: Restrict network access using Private Endpoint / VNet or firewall rules and disable public network access for production clusters when possible.
practices.prior_belief: Use network security controls: restrict access with VNet/private endpoints or IP whitelists, and prefer private networking over public endpoints for production clusters.

practices.practice: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID / managed identities and Key Vault for secrets and short-lived credentials; rotate credentials and avoid baking long-lived secrets in apps.
practices.prior_belief: Store and rotate credentials/key material with least privilege: prefer Azure AD-managed identities or Key Vault secrets and rotate keys regularly instead of baking long-lived secrets into apps or containers.

practices.practice: Do not log raw embeddings, transaction PII, or DB credentials in application logs; redact or omit sensitive fields from telemetry and agent explanations.
practices.prior_belief: Do not log raw embeddings, transaction PII, or DB credentials in application logs; redact sensitive fields in any stored agent explanations or telemetry.

practices.practice: Benchmark vector search latency and recall (p95 latency, recall@k) on representative queries and use those results to guide index and query parameter tuning.
practices.prior_belief: Benchmark vector search latency/recall for representative queries and capture metrics (p95 latency, recall@k, throughput); drive index and query parameter tuning from these benchmarks.

practices.practice: Store embedding-model metadata (model name, version, dims, and optionally version/id) with each inserted vector so re-embedding and audits are possible.
practices.prior_belief: Version and store embedding-model metadata with each inserted vector (model name, model version, tokenizer options) so later re-embeddings or comparisons are auditable and consistent.

practices.practice: Use MongoDB sessions and multi-document transactions only when the cluster supports them and you need atomic multi-document semantics; otherwise prefer idempotent single-document writes.
practices.prior_belief: Use MongoDB sessions and transactions for multi-document atomic operations only if the cluster supports multi-document transactions and you need atomicity; otherwise design idempotent single-document writes.
practices.source_name: Use Multi-document transactions in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB

practices.practice: Use TTL (expireAfterSeconds) indexes for ephemeral data, ensure the indexed field is a Date type, and understand that the TTL sweeper runs roughly each 60s (not second-accurate).
practices.prior_belief: Use TTL indexes for ephemeral data such as temporary caches, short-lived explanations, or staging inserts to automatically reclaim storage (create index on a datetime field with expireAfterSeconds).

practices.practice: Limit the candidate set (topK) used to compute scores; compute fraud risk from a small set of nearest neighbors (e.g., top 5–10) rather than scoring very large neighbor sets returned from vector search.
practices.prior_belief: Limit topK and post-filter search results in the app logic: compute a fraud risk score from a small set of nearest neighbors (e.g., top 10) and avoid returning or scoring on very large neighbor sets.

practices.practice: Persist provenance for model decisions by storing which embedding version and which documents matched (document ids and similarity/searchScore) alongside the computed fraud score and explanation for reproducibility and audit.
practices.prior_belief: Persist provenance for model or agent decisions: store which embedding version and which documents matched (ids and distances) alongside the fraud risk score and explanation so results are reproducible and auditable.

practices.practice: Enable and test backups/restore and HA for production clusters; understand automatic backup retention windows and test restore procedures for the collections that contain vectors and metadata.
practices.prior_belief: Plan for backups and restores: ensure point-in-time restore or scheduled backups are enabled for production clusters and test restore procedures for the collection storing vectors and metadata.

practices.practice: When you need to shard, pick a shard key that avoids hot partitions (use a hashed high-cardinality field for write-heavy workloads and align shard-key selection with query patterns for read-heavy workloads).
practices.prior_belief: When designing partition/shard keys for scale, choose keys that avoid hot partitions (e.g., hashed account_id or tenant id) and ensure vectors and their metadata that are queried together land in the same logical partition where possible.

practices.practice: Vectors must be a number[] in documents to be indexed by a cosmosSearch vector index; using other types prevents indexing and those documents won't be returned by vector search.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector search type requirements

practices.practice: When using $search with cosmosSearch, project the search score via {$meta: 'searchScore'} and use returnStoredSource:true if you need the matched document returned together with the score for reranking or explanations.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Use product quantization and oversampling (or half-precision indexing) to reduce vector-index memory footprint while using oversampling in queries to preserve recall when using compressed indexes.
practices.source_name: Product quantization for vector search in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB product quantization oversampling guidance

practices.practice: Create a vector index using the createIndexes command with cosmosSearchOptions (kind, dimensions, similarity and algorithm settings) rather than copying Atlas-specific syntax; use listIndexes/getIndexes to verify index definitions.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
